title: 'Flock Flocked up'

reading.body:
This is a false-positive failure at the front end of a deployment: an automated licence plate reader asserted a match that was not there, and the alert was treated as fact by the officers who received it. The camera's own image showed a different vehicle, a Chevy Malibu, while the plate it reported belonged to a red Dodge Ram. The error was in the reading, not in any decision made downstream of it.

The failure surfaced in the field, at the point where a system output becomes a police action. Nothing in the reporting shows a human verifying the alert against the image before officers approached with guns drawn, and the plate was only confirmed as not stolen after the stop. Catching this would have required a check at the moment of the alert, comparing the flagged plate to the vehicle the camera actually photographed, or a confirmation step before the stop escalated.

What is not established is how the misread occurred, whether the system had a known error rate, or whether any policy governed verification of its alerts. The department's investigation found no wrongdoing in the K-9 use, and charges were later dropped, but neither outcome speaks to the accuracy of the camera.

reports.title: Body cam of TPD officers releasing K-9 on man during traffic stop
Man speaks out after police release K-9 on him during traffic stop: 'Traumatized'
TPD investigation finds no wrongdoing in use of K-9 on man during traffic stop
Charges dropped against man Toledo Police released K-9 on during traffic stop, lawyer says

summary:
Toledo Police released body camera video showing officers stopping a red Dodge Ram pickup after a FLOCK camera wrongly flagged its plate as stolen. The camera image belonged to a Chevy Malibu, but the plate was misread. Officers approached with guns drawn and told driver Brandon Upchurch to get out. He exited with his hands up, then walked onto the grass, and a K-9 was released. He was arrested and charged with resisting arrest and obstruction.

Officers later confirmed the plate was not stolen and that the alert was a misread. Upchurch received medical attention at the scene. Police said they believed he might flee and did not know if he or his passenger had weapons. The article does not say what happens next.
